extracted.intended_audience: public relations professionals and PR agencies
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for creating and distributing news releases/online PR content so they comply with new Google search quality expectations while still earning media and brand awareness. Emphasizes content quality, targeted distribution, relationships with journalists, and client education.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unique, relevant content that can naturally gain popularity
rubrics_metrics.description: "unique, relevant content that can naturally gain popularity in the Internet community"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Google favors unique, relevant content; PR should continue producing material that genuinely interests online communities rather than gaming algorithms. "Good PR is still good PR... Keep up the good work."

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid keyword stuffing / restrict keywords
rubrics_metrics.description: Restriction on keywords to avoid keyword stuffing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure keywords are used naturally and sparingly; avoid over-optimizing releases or blog posts purely to manipulate search rankings. The page notes most firms already comply when they include blogs in their efforts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid mass/spammy distribution; be strategic and targeted
rubrics_metrics.description: Distribution of news content must be strategic and targeted, rather than a simple push of a button to reach hundreds of markets all at once.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not blast identical releases en masse across many outlets. Tailor distribution plans to specific markets and outlets to avoid being classified as spam under Google's guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personalized pitching and audience-tailored messaging
rubrics_metrics.description: Contacting a reporter or editor to personally pitch a story and carefully crafting the message to make sure it fits the expectations of that audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain traditional media-relations skills: read target outlets, research contacts, and customize pitches so the story matches the outlet and journalist's beats and expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit links; avoid links added solely to boost rankings
rubrics_metrics.description: News pieces written for online sharing will need to contain fewer links that exist only to rev up page rankings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include only relevant, high-quality links. "Focus on limited links for greater link authority." Applies to news releases, longer articles, guest blogs, and other online content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Write engaging, consumer-focused content rather than promotional copy
rubrics_metrics.description: Pieces should be written as engaging, clever pieces that consumers want to read while they boost awareness for brands 'naturally.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid overtly promotional language; create stories that provide value or interest to readers so sharing and attention are earned rather than forced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid being overly promotional
rubrics_metrics.description: It could take some adjustment to be sure pieces are not overly 'promotional.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review content for promotional tone and reduce marketing-heavy phrasing. Aim for journalistic or editorial value where appropriate so content isn't downgraded by search or editorial gatekeepers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish agency parameters to protect clients' compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: PR agencies may need to establish their own new parameters for protecting clients from falling outside of the guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop internal policies, approval workflows, and distribution standards to ensure client releases and content meet search engine and media expectations; this will require effort and decision-making.

rubrics_metrics.name: Educate clients with step-by-step strategies and set expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: With the right information provided to them about your step-by-step strategies, clients will likely enjoy and appreciate the opportunity for more targeted and specific results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proactively explain changes in approach (e.g., targeted distribution, link strategy, tone) to clients so they understand and accept potential trade-offs for better long-term visibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus on the right story, to the right audience, in the right format
rubrics_metrics.description: Focusing on the right story to the right audience in the right format still works, whether it’s about crisis management, reputation management or social media communication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Match content type and channel to the story and audience (e.g., crisis messaging vs. thought leadership). Strategic alignment across story, audience, and format remains central to successful PR under the guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain and deepen relationships with key newsroom contacts
rubrics_metrics.description: PR executives may need to seek out and really get to know key newsroom contacts – which, again, the best never stopped doing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Invest time in cultivating reporter/editor relationships; personalized outreach and knowledge of newsroom needs help secure placements without relying on mass distribution or SEO tricks.
